prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] Rebuild Hokusai's "Great Wave off Kanagawa" as a single-file low-poly 3D scene with gentle motion, plus a result.json recording what was taken from the print.

[action] Inspected ./print.jpg (Hokusai, public domain). Built ./scene/index.html: Three.js r170 from the allowed CDN, everything in code — no texture. Composition copied: one great curling wave arcing from the left with claw foam, a mirrored wave on the right, a foreground wave; snow-capped Mt. Fuji low center-right; three rowing boats (one under the great wave, one before Fuji, one foreground); washi-paper background with flat clouds. Palette taken from the print: deep Prussian blue, mid/light blue, white foam, Fuji blue-grey + snow, warm wood hulls. Motion: waves bob/sway, boats rock, clouds drift. Wrote ./result.json with boats count and mountain name. Verified by opening the file in a browser (loads, renders, no build step); fixed foam to read white (MeshBasicMaterial). Closed the browser tab.

[result]
- ./scene/index.html — single file, only external deps are the three.js CDN (and no Google Fonts needed). Renders correctly in a browser.
- ./result.json — boats: 3; mountain: Mount Fuji (Fuji-san).

[evidence] Browser screenshots across 4 iterations: first version had disjointed gray foam boxes; rewrote waves as continuous curling ribbons; foam stayed gray under flat shading, so switched foam to unlit MeshBasicMaterial — final screenshot shows bright white foam tips on blue curling waves, snow-capped Fuji center-right, three boats, washi background. The print is recognizable at a glance.

[assumptions] "Gentle motion" = slow bob/rock/drift, no camera movement. Low-poly = box/cone primitives, flat-shaded. The print's exact claw detail is simplified to foam-tip clusters; the brief asks for recognizability, not a replica.

[what I found / how I know it is right] The print is Hokusai's *Kanagawa oki nami ura* (Great Wave off Kanagawa), c. 1831 — identifiable by the towering left wave with claw foam, the small snow-capped Fuji to the right of center, and the three long fishing boats. I confirmed by reading the image directly. The scene mirrors those three anchors (wave, Fuji, 3 boats) in the print's palette, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it. I know the file works because I opened it in a browser and saw the rendered scene; the only network dependency is the allowed three.js CDN.

[next] None — deliverables are complete and verified. Browser closed.
